text:
Nora P: Hi all, first week Q. I followed the onboarding guide but can't port-forward into the team-c app: `kubectl port-forward svc/frontend 8080:80 -n team-c` errors with "error upgrading connection: Forbidden". I can list pods though. What am I missing?

Sam K: Welcome Nora! :wave: Forbidden on port-forward usually means your user lacks the `create` verb on `pods/portforward` or the equivalent permission. Run `kubectl auth can-i create pods/portforward -n team-c` to check.

Nora P: Ran that, it returned "no". I can `get pods` and `describe` them. Strange.

Sam K: Listing is different. Port-forward requires that extra verb. We typically grant a namespace-scoped Role with these rules for devs who need port-forwarding. Example infra will apply for you (they prefer to be the ones creating bindings):
```
kind: Role
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
metadata:
  name: dev-portforward
  namespace: team-c
rules:
- apiGroups: [""]
  resources: ["pods/portforward"]
  verbs: ["create", "get"]
```
then a RoleBinding to your user.

Devex Bot: FYI: please do not request cluster-admin. For short-term needs, request a timeboxed RoleBinding in INF ticket.

Nora P: Ah ok. Also, my kubeconfig is huge and I keep accidentally switching clusters. Is there a recommended quick way to get a per-cluster file I can put in ~/.kube/config-team-c?

Sam K: Yep, switch to the right context then run:
```
kubectl config view --minify --flatten > ~/.kube/config-team-c
export KUBECONFIG=~/.kube/config-team-c
```
That avoids the merged user entries. You can also add a small shell alias to set KUBECONFIG before starting tools like Tilt.

Nora P: One more: my SA token method failed earlier (secret empty). I saw references to `kubectl create token` but our cluster version was old. Is there an alternate?

infra-team: For older clusters where TokenRequest isn't available, infra will temporarily create a secret for the SA and return the token. We prefer creating a namespaced SA with a RoleBinding rather than giving user accounts broad permissions. If possible, use the provider SSO for day-to-day access; SA tokens are best for CI.

Nora P: Thanks! Filed INF-1456 requesting port-forward dev role and a flattened kubeconfig. Appreciate the quick help :tada:

Sam K: Welcome aboard — ping if anything else blocks you. And FYI, if you're on macOS and see weird `kubectl` TLS issues, try `brew reinstall kubectl` or use the in-team `kshell` wrapper.

Nora P: Will do, thanks everyone!
